react_result.final_narrative_text: The seven differentially abundant metabolites converge on a single dominant biological theme: steroid hormone biosynthesis and metabolism. Three independent enrichment paradigms return the same pathway as their top hit with exceptional consistency. KEGG:hsa00140 (Steroid hormone biosynthesis and estrogen/androgen metabolism) is ranked #2 in RaMP multi-DB ORA (FDR = 2.93e-15, fold enrichment = 1667.9, 5/27 metabolites hit), ranked #0 in MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA (p = 2.51e-06, 5/87 metabolites hit), and ranked #0 in Mummichog's empirical-compound network (p = 8.40e-05, 11/11 metabolites hit — a complete-pathway overrepresentation). In the Mummichog result the matching pathway is explicitly labelled 'Androgen and estrogen biosynthesis and metabolism' and captures all five input steroids plus six structurally adjacent intermediates (androsterone, 5α-androstane-3,17-dione, estriol, and others). The five driver steroids are estrone (CHEBI:17263), dehydroepiandrosterone (CHEBI:28689), testosterone (CHEBI:17347), 17β-estradiol (CHEBI:16469), and 17β-hydroxy-5α-androstan-3-one / dihydrotestosterone (CHEBI:16330). Their InChIKey first-blocks (DNXHEGUUPJUMQT, FMGSKLZLMKYGDP, MUMGGOZAMZWBJJ, VOXZDWNPVJITMN, NVKAWKQGWWIWPM) are mutually consistent and map to three enzyme reactions in the KEGG graph: CYP19A1 (aromatase, estrone ↔ 17β-estradiol), HSD17B (17β-hydroxysteroid dehydrogenases), and HSD3B/17,20-lyase steps in the C19→C18 steroid transition. Guanidoacetic acid (C00581, InChIKey BPMFZUMJYQTVII, the immediate creatine precursor) appears in guanidinoacetic acid / glycine-serine metabolism pathways at sub-threshold p-values in both MetaboAnalystR and Mummichog, suggesting a secondary perturbation of arginine–glycine transamidination distinct from the steroid axis. The cross-paradigm consensus on KEGG:hsa00140 / 'Androgen and Estrogen Metabolism' with a unified set of five driver steroids defines a robust, biologically coherent narrative of coordinated steroidogenic disruption.

react_result.final_narrative_text: The seven differentially abundant metabolites converge on two biologically distinct themes. The dominant signal is an exceptionally strong enrichment of five C18/C19 steroids—estrone, dehydroepiandrosterone, testosterone, 17β-estradiol, and 17β-hydroxy-5α-androstan-3-one (dihydrotestosterone)—across multiple independent enrichment paradigms. RaMP multi-DB ORA identifies '17-Beta Hydroxysteroid Dehydrogenase III Deficiency' (SMPDB:SMP00356) as its top hit with FDR = 2.93e-15, fold enrichment = 1667.9, and 5 of 27 pathway members detected. The same five steroids produce the identical top-rank hit in 'Androgen and Estrogen Metabolism' (SMPDB:SMP00068) and its KEGG counterpart (KEGG:map00150), indicating that the RaMP consensus on the steroid axis is robust across three database namespaces. MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA ranks KEGG:hsa00140 first with p = 2.51e-06, and Mummichog's empirical-compound network returns 'Androgen and estrogen biosynthesis and metabolism' (MUMM:androgen_and_estrogen_biosynthesis_and_metabolism) as its top hit with p = 8.40e-05 and 11 of 11 pathway members matched—complete pathway overrepresentation. Guanidoacetic acid is a secondary signal appearing in 'Glycine, serine, alanine and threonine metabolism' (MUMM:glycine_serine_alanine_and_threonine_metabolism) at p = 0.0396, consistent with its role as the immediate creatine precursor. N-Acetylgalactosamine is resolved as N-acetyl-D-glucosamine in the Mummichog network and appears in 'Sialic acid metabolism' and 'Hyaluronan Metabolism' at the same p-value threshold.

{
  "narrative_text": "Seven metabolites were identified as significantly differentially abundant between control and treatment groups. The dominant differential signal is an exceptionally coherent enrichment of five C18/C19 steroids: estrone, dehydroepiandrosterone, testosterone, 17β-estradiol, and dihydrotestosterone. RaMP multi-DB ORA identifies Androgen and Estrogen Metabolism (KEGG:map00150, FDR = 2.93e-15, 5 of 27 pathway members matched) as the top cross-database hit, sharing the same FDR and identical hit-set with its SMPDB analogue SMPDB:SMP00068. The same five steroids enrich Metabolism of steroid hormones (REACT:R-HSA-196071, FDR = 1.67e-14, 5 of 39) in the Reactome namespace. Mummichog confirms this signal independently via m/z-direct networking, returning Androgen and estrogen biosynthesis and metabolism (MUMM:androgen_and_estrogen_biosynthesis_and_metabolism, p = 8.40e-05, 11 of 11 matched) as its top hit with complete overlap. Cross-paradigm consensus converges on an androgen/estrogen axis as the dominant treatment-related perturbation. A secondary weaker signal from guanidoacetic acid is captured by Mummichog as a member of Glycine, serine, alanine and threonine metabolism (MUMM:glycine_serine_alanine_and_threonine_metabolism, p = 0.044) and Urea cycle/amino group metabolism (MUMM:urea_cycle_amino_group_metabolism, p = 0.044), where it serves as a substrate for arginine:glycine amidinotransferase (AGAT, R00627). N-acetylgalactosamine (KEGG:C01074) resolves to N-acetyl-D-glucosamine (ChEBI:506227) in the m/z network and appears as a hit in both Hyaluronan Metabolism (MUMM:hyaluronan_metabolism, p = 0.044) and Sialic acid metabolism (MUMM:sialic_acid_metabolism, p = 0.044).",

The dominant differential signal is an exceptionally coherent enrichment of five C18/C19 steroids: estrone, dehydroepiandrosterone, testosterone, 17β-estradiol, and dihydrotestosterone. RaMP multi-DB ORA identifies Androgen and Estrogen Metabolism (KEGG:map00150, FDR = 2.93e-15, 5 of 27 pathway members matched) as the top cross-database hit, sharing the same FDR and identical hit-set with its SMPDB analogue SMPDB:SMP00068. The same five steroids enrich Metabolism of steroid hormones (REACT:R-HSA-196071, FDR = 1.67e-14, 5 of 39) in the Reactome namespace. Mummichog confirms this signal independently via m/z-direct networking, returning Androgen and estrogen biosynthesis and metabolism (MUMM:androgen_and_estrogen_biosynthesis_and_metabolism, p = 8.40e-05, 11 of 11 matched) as its top hit with complete overlap. Cross-paradigm consensus converges on an androgen/estrogen axis as the dominant treatment-related perturbation. A secondary weaker signal from guanidoacetic acid is captured by Mummichog as a member of Glycine, serine, alanine and threonine metabolism (MUMM:glycine_serine_alanine_and_threonine_metabolism, p = 0.044) and Urea cycle/amino group metabolism (MUMM:urea_cycle_amino_group_metabolism, p = 0.044), where it serves as a substrate for arginine:glycine amidinotransferase (AGAT, R00627). N-acetylgalactosamine (KEGG:C01074) resolves to N-acetyl-D-glucosamine (ChEBI:506227) in the m/z network and appears as a hit in both Hyaluronan Metabolism (MUMM:hyaluronan_metabolism, p = 0.044) and Sialic acid metabolism (MUMM:sialic_acid_metabolism, p = 0.044).
